//: Editor excludes for a workspace whose root holds ~400 GB of simulation output. Measured 2026-08-23:
runs 310G, runs_seed_aars 44G, runs_kinetic_seeds 25G, runs_depleting 18G, refit_sweep 2.7G,
.venv 1.2G, runs_codeonly 709M.
pyrightconfig.json already scopes TYPE ANALYSIS to first-party code. This file covers the two things it
does not: the FILE WATCHER and SEARCH.
files.watcherExclude is the important one, and it is not covered by .gitignore. VS Code's watcher does
not read .gitignore — only search does, via search.useIgnoreFiles. So even though runs/ and friends are
gitignored, the watcher was still registering recursive handles over a 310 GB tree. On Windows that
costs handles and CPU; on Linux it exhausts inotify watches outright.
refit_sweep/ (2.7G), parca4_work/, vendor/ and archive/ are NOT gitignored — they are working artefacts
that were never meant to be indexed either, and vendor/ + archive/ additionally carry duplicate copies of
the wcEcoli package layout, which is the auto-import hazard pyrightconfig.json exists to stop.
TYPE CHECKING OFF, matching pyrightconfig.json. The first version of these files set 'basic', which
turned a type checker on across a codebase that was never annotated for one — ~20 files lit up at once,
and every case read was correct code the checker simply cannot prove. Scoping the indexer and enabling a
type checker are separate decisions; only the first was the point. ruff is the linter here and runs in CI.
model_overlay/ is deliberately NOT in search.exclude or files.watcherExclude, though it IS excluded from
ANALYSIS. Its cleaned/, authored/ and files/ trees are live, hand-edited source that build_model_overlay.py
reads and apply_model_overlay.py ships. Hiding them from Ctrl+Shift+F would hide real code. Excluding them
from analysis is enough to stop auto-import binding a symbol to the wrong copy, which was the actual
hazard. vendor/ and archive/ are dead copies and are excluded from everything.
